clue.text: Penned in, unable to protect king

definitions.meaning: held under restraint, confined or controlled
in chess, a king held in check is threatened and the player must deal with it

explanation.surface: A chess player, boxed in, finds their king under attack with no defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves define the phrase: one is the everyday idiom for restraint, the other its literal chess sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means restrained, and in chess a king under threat is said to be in check.

clue.text: Humiliatingly dismiss at start of game

definitions.meaning: to throw someone out roughly and without ceremony
the opening kick that begins a football match

explanation.surface: A player is sent off in disgrace right as the match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Booting someone out is a rude dismissal, and the opening kick begins a football match.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a fielding position square of the batsman on the off side
aim or object, as in 'what is the ...?'

explanation.surface: A cricketer in the field displays determination.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a cricket fielding position, and by extension the player standing there.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket position names its player, and an aim or object is what something is for.

clue.text: In a social function, very involved ahead of time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the very word is wrapped up inside the social function

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: Someone gets deeply caught up in a party before it has even started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' signals one piece wrapped inside another; 'very involved' reads like a surface phrase about getting caught up, which hides the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something beforehand means doing it early, before the time it is needed.

definitions.meaning: a cage or pen for poultry

explanation.surface: A store that has chickens on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British chain of co-operative grocery stores.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-operative is a member-owned store, and a poultry cage houses chickens.

parts.note: the saying goes that this large animal of Africa never forgets

explanation.surface: Someone born in Africa recalls the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remembering' looks like a verb about a person, but it points to the proverbial memory of the beast with a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tusked beast of the savanna is proverbially said never to forget.

parts.note: a spit is also a skewer, so this food is cooked or served on a spit

explanation.surface: A dish so unpleasant one may want to spit it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit out' suggests rejecting food in disgust; the spit is really the skewer of grilled meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered grilled meat is cooked on a spit, the rod that turns over a fire.

parts.note: winds means turns round, as a spring is wound
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone spins about on a golden seat.
explanation.walkthrough: A WINDSOR chair is a traditional wooden chair with a spindle back.
explanation.definitionFit: The spindle-backed wooden seat named after the Berkshire town is a classic style of chair.

definitions.meaning: the total sales income of a business
a pastry folded over a fruit filling, like the apple kind

explanation.surface: Cash is handed over in exchange for a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's gross sales are its income, and a folded pastry with filling is a small pie.

clue.text: Moving one's chair to see flower

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shifts their seat to get a better view of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges ONESCHAIR (the letters of 'one's chair').
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese hibiscus is a showy tropical shrub grown for its blooms.

indicators.note: following, so this word comes after the other

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ruin means disaster

explanation.surface: Catastrophe chases a dark-coated bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' puts RUIN after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional folk name for the brown animal of fable.

indicators.note: the greeting is placed following the month

parts.note: OCT is the short form of October
ave is Latin for hail

explanation.surface: A salutation arrives once a month's gap has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the Latin salutation behind the month even though the clue names it first. 'interval' is the musical sense, a span of eight notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the span of eight notes between a pitch and its double is an interval.

clue.text: But diver may suffer these, coming straight up

definitions.text: But diver may suffer these, coming straight up

parts.words: But diver may suffer these, coming straight up
parts.note: a diver rising too fast gets decompression sickness, ironically named for curves although the ascent is straight

explanation.surface: A diver who surfaces too directly risks decompression sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'But' points at the irony: the illness is named after curves, yet it comes from going straight up.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness strikes divers who surface too fast, named for the doubled-up posture of sufferers.

clue.text: Productive sum of money city held

indicators.note: the sum of money holds the city inside it

parts.note: a fund is a sum of money set aside
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A city kept a pot of cash that turned out to be fruitful.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile and fruitful mean producing abundantly.

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means swiftly

explanation.surface: A car speeds along using its protective casing.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper casing of a turtle or crab is its protective covering.

parts.note: a raver goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted Englishman who loves a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incisive' looks like sharp-minded, but it means cutting into a surface, as an artisan does with a burin.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan who cuts designs into metal or wood makes incisions for a living.

clue.text: Bad liar — press acts in retaliation

indicators.note: the letters are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A dishonest person and the newspapers strike back at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges LIARPRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliatory measures are acts of revenge against an opponent.

explanation.surface: It is essential to judge with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial and decisive share one word with fault-finding or discerning judgement.

clue.text: Fords here perhaps for a way across the water

definitions.text: Fords here perhaps for a way across the water

parts.words: Fords here perhaps for a way across the water
parts.note: Ford is a make of motor, and this vessel carries such motors over the sea

explanation.surface: Shallow river crossings offer a route over water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fords' looks like river crossings, but it is the car maker; 'perhaps' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that transports motor vehicles over a channel or strait.

clue.text: Clubs being beaten and going out of business

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
losing means being beaten

explanation.surface: Sports clubs on a losing streak are shutting down.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop shutting for good is ending its trading.

clue.text: Old Greek state to practise fighting with volunteers

parts.note: boxers spar in practice bouts
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior state trains its citizen-soldiers for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The warlike city-state of the Peloponnese was a rival of Athens.

clue.text: Almost bound to be a diplomat

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: attached means bound or tied

explanation.surface: Someone nearly tied to a post serves as an envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final D from ATTACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy official assigned to a specialist area is a junior member of a diplomatic staff.

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or mate
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A pal owns a plot right over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is British informal slang for a mate or partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing, on the other side, describes something straight across from another.

indicators.note: the word's extremes, its first and last letters, are taken

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A pointed nail comes with the right tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a small headless tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A small headless tack used by glaziers is a kind of brad or pin.

clue.text: Disclose if rejected for a cut of meat

indicators.note: turned back, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: to tell is to disclose

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to reveal whether a steak was sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TELLIF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneless strip of beef or fish is a prime cut.

clue.text: Trainee priest is a woolly type

parts.note: L is the learner, as on British L-plates
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A novice cleric turns out to be a shaggy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign on British cars driven by trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean beast of burden has a long fleecy coat.

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A card is marked in a club game.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for the mark, the former German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy spiked staff is a weapon like a cudgel.

indicators.note: rendering the word into other terms reorders its letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the job of decoding ancient runes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges RUNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a cost or debt is to bring it upon oneself.

parts.note: the name comes from French words meaning carriage with benches

explanation.surface: A trainer who works in the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' reads as a trainer, but it is a sightseeing bus, from French char à bancs.
explanation.definitionFit: The old open sightseeing bus takes its name from the French for a carriage with benches.

indicators.note: the letters are manoeuvred into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Clever lawful tactics rescue a former prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvres' rearranges LEGALLYSAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners were once sentenced to row in warships, chained to the oars.
